steps.step: Fix the interface this UI plans against (model area owns the implementation)
steps.where: js/moves.js:1226-1231 PLANNERS/RESOLVERS; a new js/deals.js registered in js/statedoc.js:77-112 and :197
steps.detail: Intent: `{type:'deal', nid, target, resource:<sector index>, volume:<$M/turn>, priceFactor:<1±band>, duration:<turns>, autoRenew:<bool>}`. `Moves.plan` returns the usual `{ok, reason, cost:0, effects[]}` plus `perTurn:{me, them}` ($M treasury per turn under these terms), `total` over the duration, `expiresTurn`, `indexPrice` (Market.getPrices()[resource]), `maxVolume` (matched flow clipped by min(capacity of both), the same arithmetic as planTrade :413-414), and `verdict:{kind:'accept'|'counter'|'decline', counter:{priceFactor, volume, duration, autoRenew}|null, changed:['duration',…], reasons:[string]}`. `verdict` must be a PURE function of world state and terms (no rng) so Propose is idempotent. `Moves.resolve` creates the deal (id from the module's own `seq`), writes the ledger kind `deal`, records Relations 'traded' once at signing, and settles nothing on the spot — the first payment is the next world tick. Deals API the UI reads: `forNation(nid)` (sorted by turnsLeft then id), `between(a,b)`, `incomePerTurn(nid)`, `waiting(player)` → the next expired player-party deal or null, `answer(dealId, 'renew'|'lapse', tune)` → `{ok, renewed, reason}`, `offersTo(nid)` (empty in A1; A4 fills it), `serialize/loadState` carrying `seq`, deals and the pending queue. `Deals.tick(tune)` is called in js/world.js immediately before :1215 `Game.tickTreasuries()`: countdown notices are checked BEFORE decrement (so a 4-turn deal produces notices at 4, 2 and 1 and expires at the end of its fourth paid turn — the only reading that satisfies spec §7 Checkpoint 3 'a 4-turn deal… countdowns at 4/2/1'), then settlement, then expiry: auto-renew re-signs on the same terms if its plan still says ok, otherwise it joins the player's queue if the player is a party or lapses with a ledger entry if not.

steps.step: The deal offer panel replaces renderTradePreview
steps.where: js/actions.js:690-751 (renderTradePreview, confirmTrade) → renderDealOffer(tid, prefill), renderDealVerdict(v), signDeal(intent); startTradeWith(me, tid, prefill) added beside startReleaseWith :1185
steps.detail: Layout, top to bottom, all with existing classes: actionHead('🚛 Trade — negotiate a deal'); hint-block naming the partner; the recognition refusal box exactly as :721-723 when `!dealsWith`; RESOURCE — the matched flows from `plan.flows` rendered as `.geo-row gov-opt[data-res]` rows (econ-dot, sector, direction '→ them'/'← us', $ value), largest selected by default, a click re-renders with that resource; VOLUME — `.slider-row` range from `deal.volumeFloor × maxVolume` to `maxVolume` (label 'of what X can take'), capacityNote (:379-389) underneath when capped; PRICE — `.slider-row` range −band..+band around the index in 1% steps, opening AT the index (0%), label 'Price: index 112 ± N%' with the $/turn effect on both treasuries updated live; DURATION — a row of four `.btn ghost` buttons (new `.dur-opts`, `.active` styled like `.ob-tab.active`), one per entry of `deal.durations`, each labelled '<n> turns · <calendar words>' where the words come from n × TUNE.peek('calendar.monthsPerTurn') (24 → 'two years'), default = `deal.defaultDuration`; AUTO-RENEW — a `label.opt` checkbox (menu.js:127 pattern) 'Renew on the same terms when it runs out'; three `.stat` blocks: 'To your treasury, per turn' (surplus/deficit colour), 'Over the whole deal' (perTurn × duration), 'Runs until' (Calendar.label(World.getTurn() + duration)); then `#deal-response`, then `.btn-row` Back / Propose. Every control's input handler re-plans, re-renders the three stats and clears `#deal-response` (the :599 rule). `prefill` (from a renegotiation) sets resource/volume/price/duration/autoRenew before the first render. Disclosure is not applied to action panels (only renderNationPanel calls it, panels.js:129), so nothing here can fold.

steps.step: Propose, and the counter-offer that can change duration
steps.where: js/actions.js renderDealVerdict, inside the offer panel's `#deal-response`
steps.detail: Propose calls `Moves.plan(intent)` and notes Telemetry 'deal-propose' {d: verdict.kind, dur: duration, res}. accept → `.deal-verdict accept` '✅ X accepts.' + `.deal-why` reasons + button 'Sign — N turns, $Y a turn' → signDeal. counter → `.deal-verdict counter` '↔️ X counters.' + a `.deal-diff` list with one row per term in `verdict.changed`: label, 'yours → theirs' (duration rows print both turns and calendar words, e.g. '8 turns · two years → 4 turns · one year'), unchanged terms greyed; two buttons: 'Accept their terms' (re-plans with `verdict.counter` — must come back accept by construction; if it does not, flash the reason as 'warn', which is a model bug surfaced honestly) and 'Adjust' (loads the counter into the sliders and the duration row and re-renders so the player can move one term and re-propose). decline → `.deal-verdict decline` '❌ X declines.' + reasons; controls stay live. Because the verdict is pure, re-proposing identical terms is a no-op, so there is no grind loop and no rng.

`Moves.resolve(intent, store.rng)`; on `!ok` flash the reason 'bad' and stay; else `A = null; clearVisuals()`, Telemetry 'deal-sign' {dur, res, autoRenew}, flash 'good': '🚛 <me> and <them> signed a <calendar words> deal — <buyer> takes <$V> of <sector> a turn at index <±N%>. First payment next quarter.' then `completeTurn()` — signing new terms is the turn's action like every other Move (DESIGN.md:498). The flash is a copy of the ledger entry the resolver wrote, per journal.js:32-34.

steps.step: The renegotiation prompt as a halt
steps.where: js/shell.js completeTurn :250-254 (one line after showCrisis); the card renderer `showRenegotiation()` in js/panels.js beside showCrisis :160-209
steps.detail: In completeTurn, after the crisis line and before `const next = you()`: `if (typeof Deals !== 'undefined' && Deals.waiting(you()) && showRenegotiation()) return true;`. Last in the chain on purpose: a breakaway, a lost election, defeat, victory and a crisis all outrank an expired contract, and only one card is shown per completeTurn (see risks). It can never fire mid-sweep because the queue is only read here, after AI.sweep :208 has returned — the same guarantee Events.waiting enjoys at :250. showRenegotiation: `const q = Deals.waiting(me)`; card = `.end-kicker` 'Expired · <Calendar.label(turn)>', `h2` '<dot> Your deal with X has run out', `.end-sub` '<sector>, $V a turn at index ±N%, <n> turns. It paid your treasury $P over its life; the index for <sector> is now <now> against the <then> it was signed at.' Then `.crisis-opts` with three `.crisis-opt`s: 'Renew on the same terms' (`.co-note`: 'Another <words>. Does not use your turn.' — disabled with the plan's reason as the note when `Moves.plan` on the old terms is not accept: partner gone, no longer bordering, nothing left to trade, or a counter), 'Renegotiate' (`.co-note`: 'Opens the table with these terms filled in. Signing new terms is your action this turn.'), 'Let it lapse' (`.co-note`: 'Nothing changes hands. You can propose again any turn.'). Handlers: Renew → `Deals.answer(id,'renew',TUNE)`, flash, `Game.touch({values:true})`, select player; Renegotiate → `Deals.answer(id,'lapse')` then `Actions.startTradeWith(me, partner, oldTerms)` (cancel from that panel simply leaves it lapsed); Lapse → `Deals.answer(id,'lapse')`, select player. After any answer, if `Deals.waiting(me)` still has an entry (two deals expired the same quarter) the card re-renders with the next before control returns — deterministic order: by deal id. Telemetry 'renegotiate' {d: choice}. All three answers go through the model (Deals.answer), never the DOM, so the queue is testable headless.

steps.step: A restored pending prompt is asked on resume
steps.where: js/app.js:339 (after `select('nation', you())`) and js/saves.js:105-109 (after the sweep in apply)
steps.detail: `if (typeof Deals !== 'undefined' && Deals.waiting(you())) showRenegotiation();` in both places. Deals.serialize carries the queue (events.js:321-322 precedent). Note: the existing code does NOT re-show a restored pending crisis at boot (grep: showCrisis is called only from shell.js:250); mirror that gap deliberately for crises is not this plan's job, but the deal prompt should not inherit it, because a lapsed deal costs money every turn it sits unanswered.

steps.step: The Deals block on the nation panel, own card and rival card
steps.where: js/panels.js renderNationPanel :71-91 (insert `renderDeals(nid)` after renderExportAccess :88); new renderDeals(nid) near renderExportAccess :921
steps.detail: OWN card (`Game.isPlayer(nid)`): `.stat` > `.label` 'Deals · <n> running' > `.value` = the COUNT ('3 deals' / 'No deals') > `.geo-row`s: one per deal, at most 5, sorted by turns left then id — '<partner> · <sector> · <±$/turn>' left, right `<strong>` '<k> turns left' with class `surplus` normally, `warn` (amber, new) at ≤ max(deal.countdownAt), `deficit` at the last one; then a `.geo-row` 'Next expiry' → Calendar.short; then a `.geo-row` 'Income from deals' → Deals.incomePerTurn. No control inside this block, so Disclosure folds it (not in DEFAULT_OPEN disclosure.js:39; slug 'deals' is stable because the live count sits after the middot, :55). The `.value` is the count, NOT the countdown, so the `.changed` marker (:131-141) fires on a signing or a lapse and not every quarter — a block that lights up every turn is the failure panels.js:797-801 warns about. A `.linklike` button 'Open the deal ledger →' is placed as its own element AFTER the block (like `#goto-current` :60), wired to `DealBook.open('active')`. RIVAL card (both modes, no politics gate): `.stat` 'Deals with you' with the pair's live deals as rows and a `.btn-row` with `.btn ghost dip` '🚛 Propose a deal' (disabled with `plan.reason` as title when `Moves.plan({type:'deal', nid: me, target: nid, …defaults})` refuses — e.g. not adjacent, no matching surplus, recognition), wired to `Actions.startTradeWith(me, nid)`. Carrying a control, it is never folded (disclosure.js:125-126), which is the renderDiplomacy precedent. Treasury block (renderTreasury, called at :73; internals not read — unverified): add one `.geo-row` 'Deals' → +$/turn when non-zero so the treasury explains its own number.

steps.where: new js/dealbook.js (`DealBook`), script tag in index.html after :111 journal.js; menu entry in js/menu.js:71-82; css/style.css new `.deal-table` rules after :723
steps.detail: Name: `DealBook`, because `Ledger` is the event ledger (ledger.js:32) and a second module called anything-Ledger would be read as the same thing. `open(tab)` guards with screenBlocked() (objectives.js:203-206), notes Telemetry 'dealbook' {d: tab}, and calls openModal(…, {wide:true}) with `.ob-tabs`: 'Running (n)' and 'On the table (m)'. RUNNING: a `.deal-table` (flex rows, `.geo-row` sized) with columns partner (color dot + name), resource (econ-dot + sector), to you / turn (surplus/deficit), price ('index ±N% · signed at 104, index now 112' — the drift that makes a long deal a bet), runs until (Calendar.short + '<k> turns left', same warn/deficit colouring as the panel block), renew (✓ auto / —). Sorted by turns left then id. Empty state: 'No deals running. Open Trade on your own card and click a neighbour.' ON THE TABLE: rows from `Deals.offersTo(me)`: from, resource, terms, 'expires in <k> turns' (`deal.offerExpiryTurns`), and Accept / Decline buttons that call the model — the table is built and wired in A1 so A4 only has to populate it; empty state in A1: 'Nothing on the table yet. Other nations start sending offers in a later build.' Footer `.modal-btns` Close (data-close). Entry points: Menu › Deals (item not gated on `off`, description 'The deal ledger — what is running, what is expiring, what is on the table.'), the `.linklike` under the panel block, a 'See the ledger' `.linklike` in the renegotiation card's `.end-sub`, and a one-line 'You have <n> deals running · ledger' in renderTradePrompt (:494-502). Read-only in A1: no cancel/breach — the addendum does not list one and inventing a breach cost would be tuning.

steps.step: Journal: two new ledger kinds and their family
steps.where: js/ledger.js:41-59 KINDS, :122-128 WEIGHT; js/journal.js:63-69 FAMILIES, :72-81 matches
steps.detail: KINDS += 'deal' (signed / renewed / lapsed / expired — the delta's sign says which, the treaty precedent at :47-49: +total over the deal on signing, −total on lapse) and 'expiring' (a countdown notice). WEIGHT: deal 12 (a standing agreement outranks a one-off transaction at 10, and sits well under treaty 34: a promise is news, a contract is a smaller one), expiring 8 (a reminder never headlines over anything that happened, but 'A quiet quarter' :150-151 gives way to it). Entries: `deal` has subject = signer, `partner` = the other side, `terms` = [{name:'Per turn', value}, {name:'Turns', value}, {name:'Price vs index', value}] so the Why rows render for free (journal.js:117-123); text uses Calendar: 'Texas and Oklahoma signed a one-year deal: Oklahoma takes $210M of Agriculture a turn at the index. Runs until June 2037.' `expiring` is written ONLY for deals the player is party to (subject = the player's nation, partner = the other side) — fifty nations' countdowns would be noise and the AI does not read the journal — text 'Your Agriculture deal with Oklahoma has 2 turns left.' FAMILIES 'world' kinds += ['deal','expiring']. matches() 'you' :75-78 gains `|| e.partner === me` so a deal the player is the counterparty to shows under 'Yours'. The dock's collapsed strip (:175-177) and pulse (:252-262) need nothing: a countdown is just the latest entry. Add a test that every Ledger.KINDS lands in exactly one family (see tests) — the invariant :59-61 claims and nothing pins.

steps.where: js/tunables.js SCHEMA, new group 'Deals' after the trade block :588-658
steps.detail: Each with label, doc > 20 chars, and min/max/step for numbers (tests/tunables.test.js:8-24). `deal.durations` kind:'array' [2,4,8,20] (doc cites D163: quarters; six months / one / two / five years); `deal.defaultDuration` 4 (1..40, step 1; doc: must be a member of deal.durations — the UI falls back to the nearest member); `deal.countdownAt` kind:'array' [4,2,1]; `deal.priceBand` 0.2 (0..1, 0.05; how far from the index the price slider reaches either way); `deal.volumeFloor` 0.1 (0..1, 0.05; the smallest share of the matched volume a deal may cover); `deal.offerExpiryTurns` 2 (1..20, 1; how long an open offer stands — A4 uses it, A1 shows it). Nothing in the UI holds a literal for any of these; the panel reads TUNE.peek for labels and TUNE.get inside plans. The counterparty's weighing constants (the deal analogue of trade.counterFloor/needScale/alignmentScale :639-653) are the model area's tunables, not listed here. The 3/turn incoming cap is A4's (Addendum §2 A4) and is not added in A1.

steps.where: js/actions.js deal panel; js/panels.js renderDeals; js/journal.js:164; model weigh function (model area)
steps.detail: Deals are core loop and never gated (complexity.js:20-21): same panel, same prompt, same DealBook, same journal kinds in both modes. What differs is only what the counterparty may hold against you: in Full mode the refusal 'X does not recognise you… a signature between two governments' (:721-723) can appear (D166 keeps the block); in Economy mode Recognition.canTrade already answers yes (D166), so the box never renders — no mode branch in the UI. The verdict's reasons must not cite relations or recognition when politics is off: resolve that INSIDE the weigh function (the D166 shape — a switched-off system does not charge for itself, answered once in the model rather than at seven call sites), so the panel prints whatever reasons it is handed. The rival-card 'Deals with you' block does not carry a politics gate (renderDiplomacy :375 does; this one deliberately does not). The journal hides only the politics chip in Economy mode (:164); 'The world' stays, so deal and expiring entries are visible in both.

steps.where: css/style.css, new rules beside :307-321 (deal verdict / slider-row) and :723 (wide modal)
steps.detail: `.dur-opts` (flex row of four `.btn ghost`, `.active` = accent fill like `.ob-tab.active`), `.deal-diff` rows (label / yours → theirs, changed rows in accent), `.deal-table` (grid or flex rows at `.geo-row` size, tabular-nums for the money and countdown columns), `.countdown.warn` amber and `.countdown.bad` = var(--bad) for the ≤ threshold rows, `.deal-why` already exists (used at :608). No new colours beyond the existing --good/--bad/--accent tokens.

'deal-propose' {d: verdict, dur, res}, 'deal-sign' {dur, res, autoRenew, rounds: proposals before signing}, 'renegotiate' {d: renew|renegotiate|lapse}, 'dealbook' {d: tab}. These are the direct instruments for Addendum §3 Q1 ('is negotiating a deal interesting, or is it a menu?' — proposals per signing, how often a counter is accepted versus adjusted) and Q4 ('do expiries create useful pressure, or just admin?' — the renew/renegotiate/lapse split). Action-open/cancel (:35,:51) already record who opened Trade and backed out.

§6: a bilateral trade is a deal — resource, volume per turn, a price against the index locked at signing, a duration of 2/4/8/20 turns, optional auto-renew; the neighbour accepts, counters (price, volume or duration) or declines; signing is the turn's action; expiry prompts renew / renegotiate / lapse, with notices at 4, 2 and 1 turns; the cooldown sentence goes; the AI's instant trade is named as the interim it is until A4. §7.7: 'Two decisions the model refuses to make for you' becomes three (the expired deal). §9: STATEFUL_MODULES gains deals. §12: the struck bullet is deleted and replaced by the honest remaining gap (no consequence for not trading — CLAUDE.md:101-102).

newTunables: deal.durations — kind:'array', [2, 4, 20 → written as [2,4,8,20]], the four durations in turns; label 'Deal durations (turns)'; doc cites D163 (a turn is a quarter: six months, one year, two years, five years).
deal.defaultDuration — 4, min 1, max 40, step 1; which duration the offer panel opens on; must be a member of deal.durations (the UI snaps to the nearest member if not).
deal.countdownAt — kind:'array', [4, 2, 1]; turns-left values at which an 'expiring' notice is written for the player's deals, checked before the turn's settlement.
deal.priceBand — 0.2, min 0, max 1, step 0.05; how far either side of the index the price slider reaches.
deal.volumeFloor — 0.1, min 0, max 1, step 0.05; the smallest share of the matched, capacity-clipped volume a deal may cover.
deal.offerExpiryTurns — 2, min 1, max 20, step 1; how many turns an open offer stands on the table (A4 populates offers; A1 renders the column).
scopeCheck: No step touches demand, supply or the price index. The offer panel READS Market.getPrices() and Market.nationSurplus (as renderTradePreview does today via Moves.plan, moves.js:332-346) and writes nothing to Market. A deal's price is a per-deal term (index × factor, locked at signing), not a change to the index, and the addendum's deferred 'per-deal price multipliers' (§4) are NOT built — the counterparty's ask is a size/need/alignment heuristic in the shape of evalTransit, not the §4.1 multiplier stack. Settlement is money only: Game.earn on both treasuries inside Deals.tick before Game.tickTreasuries (world.js:1215); no Market.update is added anywhere — the world tick's own reprice at :1216 runs as it always has. One thing to say loudly, though it is the model area's call and not a blocker for this plan: if the settlement rule becomes buyer-PAYS-seller rather than the existing both-sides-earn `total × trade.gain` (moves.js:418, 442-446), that is a behaviour change to the existing economy's fiscal flows and tests/trade.test.js:68-91 ('gives the structurally-deficit nations a recovery path') would need re-reading. Recommended so as not to touch the economy: keep both-sides-earn and let the price factor SHIFT the two shares (seller × (1+p), buyer × (1−p)) so the total stays what a trade pays today.
determinism: Deal ids come from a module-level `seq` counter that Deals.serialize/loadState carry, exactly as Ledger does (ledger.js:33-35, 71, 200-205) and Relations does (relations.js:109) — never from the rng, never from Date. Deals are held in a Map keyed by id; every iteration that mutates or logs (settlement, countdown notices, expiry, the renegotiation queue, the ledger tables) sorts `[...deals.values()]` by id before walking it, so insertion history cannot decide who is paid or asked first. The renegotiation queue is drained in id order and one card at a time. The counterparty's verdict is a pure function of world state and the offered terms (no rng, no Date, no DOM reads), so Propose is idempotent and 'Accept their terms' re-plans to the same answer; the UI never draws from store.rng (the transit path does not either, :603-634), and `Moves.resolve` receives store.rng only for signature parity with the other resolvers. Ledger entries are appended in that same order, so the journal text is byte-identical between two runs of the same seed with the same scripted answers. The prompt is read only after AI.sweep returns (shell.js:208 → :250+), so whether the world ticked inside the sweep or at :201 makes no difference to what is queued. tests/world-fixture.js:187-214 fingerprint already covers treasuries, prices and turn order, so a divergence in settlement shows up in the existing same-seed invariant; a Deals.serialize deepEqual is added beside it.
risks: Two instruments coexist in A1: the player signs standing deals while the AI keeps the instant `trade` Move with a 3-turn cooldown (moves.js:1298-1300, ai.js:315-325). Until A4 the world is asymmetric — AI nations get lump sums, the player gets streams — and Addendum §3 Q6 ('does the world feel alive with AI nations trading') is measured on a stopgap. Alternative for the orchestrator to weigh: make an untermed `trade` intent resolve as a 2-turn deal at the index with no auto-renew, which converts the AI with no change to ai.js or the legal() list — but it changes AI cash flow and is a model decision, not a UI one.

Only one halt card per completeTurn (shell.js:230-250 each `return true`). A deal that expires on the same quarter as a breakaway, an election or a crisis is shown the NEXT completeTurn, after one unpaid quarter. Acceptable for alpha; note that a restored pending crisis is not re-shown at boot either (no showCrisis call in app.js/saves.js — grep), so the deal prompt is deliberately given the boot hook the crisis lacks.

The price is locked at signing and the index drifts; over 20 turns a tester will see a deal paying far from the index and may report a bug. The panel block, the DealBook row and the renegotiation card all print 'signed at <then> · index now <now>' so the bet is legible; if that is not enough, it is a copy change, not a mechanic.

The verdict reads Relations in Full mode; Relations is not gated by the politics flag (world.js:1170 runs Relations.forget unconditionally; only the RENDERING at panels.js:428 is gated). If the weigh function reads it in Economy mode the player is judged on a hidden variable — hence the D166-shaped rule that the model answers 'no relations term' when politics is off. Model area must honour it.

The slider opens at the index. D31/`trade.openingOfferFactor` (:654-658) records that a slider opening where the neighbour says yes 89% of the time contributes nothing. The deal panel has three levers (price, volume, duration) so the counter has room to bite on the other two, and 'deal-propose' telemetry will show the accept-first-try rate; if it is near 1.0 that is a tuning finding for the alpha, not something to pre-tune (CLAUDE.md:81).

Disclosure's `.changed` marker compares the `.value` text (disclosure.js:131-141). If the block's value were the countdown, it would light every quarter and teach the player to ignore it (panels.js:797-801). The plan puts the count in `.value` and the countdown in a `.geo-row`; anyone 'improving' that later re-creates the failure.

Ledger growth: `deal` entries are written for every signing and every lapse/renewal on the whole board (the AI's instant trades already write one per signing, so this is at most a doubling of that stream), `expiring` only for the player. ledger.cap is 4000 (tunables.js:524-528); a 60-turn game stays inside it, but a 200-round fast-forward with fifty nations dealing every turn would start trimming. Watch it, do not tune it.

A counter that returns a duration not in `deal.durations` (a model bug) would leave the segmented row with no active button; the UI snaps to the nearest member and prints the model's number in the diff row so the discrepancy is visible rather than hidden.

tests/moves.test.js:389 pins the legal() type list without `deal`; if the model area adds `deal` candidates to legal() in A1 rather than A4, that test and ai.test.js's kind assertion both need the new entries in the same commit.
tests: Every Ledger.KINDS entry lands in exactly one Journal.FAMILIES family and 'deal' and 'expiring' are in the 'world' family, so the 'All is the sum of the others' claim at journal.js:59-61 is pinned and a future kind cannot be forgotten.
Ledger.WEIGHT carries every kind in KINDS (deal 12, expiring 8) so a new kind cannot fall to the default 1 and vanish from headlines by accident.

A 4-turn deal signed at turn t writes 'expiring' entries with subject = the player's nation at exactly the ticks where turns-left is 4, 2 and 1 (before settlement) and no others, then lands in Deals.waiting(player) after the fourth paid tick.
An 8-turn deal writes notices at 4, 2 and 1 only, and a 2-turn deal at 2 and 1 only, driven by deal.countdownAt rather than by literals (change the tunable, watch the notices move).

Deals.waiting(player) is null before and after five AI.round calls in a fixture where no deal involves the player, and is null throughout a Sim.run (no player is seated headlessly), so the simulator and fast-forward never stall on a prompt nobody can answer.

After AI.round takes a round over the expiry of a player-party deal, Deals.waiting(player) returns that deal, and Deals.answer(id, 'lapse') empties it; answering 'renew' re-signs on identical terms with a new id and a 'deal' ledger entry, and refuses with a sentence when the partner no longer borders the player.
Two player-party deals expiring the same tick are surfaced by Deals.waiting in ascending id order, one at a time.

Moves.plan({type:'deal', …}) is pure: two calls with the same terms return deepEqual verdicts, and fingerprint() is unchanged across the call; the verdict's counter (when present) re-plans to 'accept'.
A counter can change duration: for a fixture pair where the model counters a 20-turn ask, verdict.changed includes 'duration' and verdict.counter.duration is a member of deal.durations.

Signing writes a 'deal' entry whose text contains Calendar.label(World.getTurn() + duration) and whose terms carry 'Per turn' and 'Turns', and records exactly one 'traded' Relations entry in each direction.
Same seed, same scripted signing and answers: two runs produce deepEqual Deals.serialize() and identical ledger texts, and the fingerprint matches — the A1 determinism pin.

StateDoc.STATEFUL_MODULES names 'Deals', the assembled document has a 'deals' key, and serialize → loadState → serialize is the identity including seq and a pending renegotiation (extend tests/saves.test.js:275-287 and the round-trip test).
Moves.legal in A1 offers no 'deal' intents (the tests/moves.test.js:389 list is unchanged), pinning that the AI's use of the new object is A4's — a test A4 deliberately flips.

Duration labels derived from calendar.monthsPerTurn read 'six months / one year / two years / five years' at the shipped calendar and change to '2 months / 4 months / 8 months / 20 months' when monthsPerTurn is set to 1 (tests/calendar.test.js style).
Every deal.* SCHEMA entry passes the existing metadata test (tests/tunables.test.js:8-24) and deal.defaultDuration is a member of deal.durations.
Deals.forNation(nid) is sorted by turns left then id, so the panel block, the DealBook table and the renegotiation queue all present the same order.
